title: For a closed immersion i:Z→T and a sheaf G on Z, the canonical source transition with coefficient i_*G is an isomorphism in every degree q.
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, p:X→S and g:T→S scheme morphisms, q an integer, i:Z→T a closed immersion, and G a sheaf of Λ-modules on the small etale site of Z. For the canonical source transition of [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions], the morphism from the degree-q source for g with coefficient i_*G to the degree-q source for i≫g with coefficient i^*i_*G is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F07, closed coefficient comparison, using 03QP and 0959

proof.text: For a closed immersion i, finite direct image is exact [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and closed pushforward is fully faithful [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful]. The Lean proof uses the already-proved cover-dense and locally full/faithful refinement of this latter statement, in Etale.UpperLowerStar.ClosedImmersion, with module coefficients.

The ordinary counit is invertible. On a complex, its componentwise image and its homotopy-category image are invertible. The derived counit factorization and the invertible exact-functor derived unit then imply the bounded-below derived counit is invertible. Consequently the derived right adjoint is fully faithful. The single complex of i_*G is isomorphic, by exactness and the single-functor comparison, to Ri_* applied to G[0]. The derived adjunction unit is therefore invertible there.

Rewrite the direct-image triangle transition as Rh_* applied to the derived unit, followed by the direct-image composition isomorphism. Prove this identity using composition-of-derived-adjunctions unit coherence, naturality of the composition isomorphism and the adjunction triangle identity. Both factors are invertible on the preceding single complex. Apply exact inverse image along p and degree-q homology to obtain the canonical source transition isomorphism.
